text:
sam_support: Hey all — customer ACME reported a spike of 429s starting ~07:10 UTC after a deploy. They say only one of their internal services is affected even though all use the same shared API key. Logs attached.

morgan_eng: Can you paste the 429 response headers? want to see which scope the quota service is returning.

sam_support: Sure — from the customer's forwarded headers:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2024 07:12:03 GMT
x-rw-rate-limit: 1000
x-rw-rate-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-reset: 1712347200
x-rw-quota-scope: org
x-rw-quota-id: org_987654
content-type: application/json
```

sam_support: They also sent a curl repro showing it reproduces from their infra but not from their laptop.

sam_support: repro curl (uses their internal proxy):

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_shared_internal" \
  -H "X-Forwarded-For: 10.1.2.3" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```

jess_ops: Interesting — header shows quota scope=org. We typically apply quota hierarchy: api_key > project > org > ip depending on config. If the service is seeing org scope, maybe the proxy strips project-level metadata so quota resolution falls back to org.

morgan_eng: Can you confirm whether the proxy is rewriting or dropping any Redwood headers? Specifically check if `x-rw-project` or `x-rw-client-id` are being forwarded.

sam_support: I asked — they said the proxy injects its own `x-rw-proxy` header and rewrites `Authorization` to a shared key, so per-service project id wouldn't make it to our gateway.

kai_infra: That matches my hunch. If the proxy normalizes to a single API key and we can't see the original project id, quota lookup will aggregate at the org level for that key. That will make one noisy service exhaust org quota.

morgan_eng: Repro steps for us: simulate identical behavior by sending requests with same `Authorization` but different `X-Forwarded-For` and with/without `x-rw-project`. If adding `x-rw-project: project_abc` removes the 429, it's a scoping artifact.

sam_support: I ran the quick test from a sandbox and saw this:

```
# no project header -> 429 and x-rw-quota-scope: org
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_shared_internal" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"text":"x"}'

# with project header -> 200 OK and x-rw-quota-scope: project
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_shared_internal" -H "x-rw-project: project_abc" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"text":"x"}'
```

jess_ops: Nice repro. So root cause = proxy rewrites to shared API key + drops project metadata. Customer is using a single shared key for multiple internal services — bad pattern for quota isolation.

morgan_eng: Two actionable fixes:
1) Customer: issue per-service API keys (or per-project keys). That ensures isolation at key scope.
2) If they must use a shared key behind the proxy, configure the proxy to forward `x-rw-project` (or `x-rw-client-id`) and preserve Authorization header identity, or enable a header that our gateway trusts for project mapping.

kai_infra: We should also check our rate limiter config: if `key_priority` is currently lower than `org_fallback` then a missing project header causes fallback to org. Temporary mitigation: bump org quota or add a rule to prefer api_key if available, but customer-side fix is preferred.

morgan_eng: I'll open a short-lived policy override for org_987654 to give them breathing room while they rotate keys. Patch: create override +10% for next 2 hours.

RateLimitBot: Policy override created: override_id=ovr_20240612_01 target=org_987654 delta_tokens=+50000 expires_at=1712353950

sam_support: Customer confirms they're going to rotate to per-service keys. They asked if we can provide a short checklist for proxies so they don't accidentally drop forwarding headers.

jess_ops: Quick checklist to send:
- Do not rewrite Authorization; forward original `Authorization` header.
- Preserve `x-rw-project`, `x-rw-client-id` if set by clients.
- If injecting a shared key is unavoidable, set a distinct `x-rw-project` per upstream service before forwarding.
- Avoid NATting all requests to single IP if you expect IP-based scoping to distinguish services.

morgan_eng: Also add: confirm with curl using `-H "x-rw-project: <id>"` that the 200s return and `x-rw-quota-scope: project` in headers.

sam_support: Shared key rotation note: customer asked whether rotating the shared key will clear the org quota impact. Answer: rotating the key will separate future requests to a new key (fresh quota bucket) but won't refund tokens spent under old key — so quota exhaustion persists until reset/override.

kai_infra: I'll follow up with a small doc snippet we can paste into the ticket with the repro curl commands and the proxy checklist.

morgan_eng: After they finish rotating keys, we should monitor their `x-rw-rate-remaining` on dashboards and watch for any further 429s. Recommend enabling per-project dashboards in Console.

sam_support: Customer reacted :thumbsup: — closing the immediate escalation. I'll attach our repro logs and the RateLimitBot override to the support ticket.

morgan_eng: Thanks everyone — good triage. :eyes:
